notes: Lead profile: mid-stage ecommerce platform - lightweight AI features embedded in checkout and customer chat. Mostly self-serve devs with small infra team.
Customer quote from 2026-02-15 call: 'Users in UK are complaining about slow chat — sessions feel laggy around checkout.'

Problem summary: primary pain = elevated request latency for EU-origin traffic hitting default us-west host. Secondary: occasional 30s timeouts in their client showing 'no response' and retries causing duplicate UI actions.

Observed metrics (SE analysis): 50th pct ~120ms, 90th ~480ms when routing through us-west; token generation time proportional to prompt length and includes network roundtrip for first token. Small spikes correlate with model selection (larger open models chosen by devs during experiment).
- Region: recommend switching to eu-west endpoint (eu-west1) for EU-heavy traffic; test via region override header or endpoint DNS rewrite. Expect ~80-140ms reduction on avg RTT.

- Timeouts: increase client-level read timeout to 60s for chat streaming flows; use streaming mode to surface early tokens and avoid full-response wait. Add exponential backoff and idempotency keys for retries.

- Prompt engineering: trim system + preface length; move static context to server-side cached embeddings where possible. Recommended target prompt body <800 tokens for interactive flows to improve per-token latency.
- Model routing: prefer smaller latency-optimized model variants for UI-facing chat (cost/lower-latency) and route long-form generation to background job endpoints.
- Batching/caching: for high-throughput embedding/rerank jobs, use batch endpoints and enable prefix KV caching for assistant conversations.
